chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: The band's shock in Baltimore and Ella following McRae
summary: After the Montgomery news, the shock hit in Baltimore, where Ella followed McRae through the streets crying.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I know he was weak, but, you know, like -- he kept saying, you know, "I'll see you later." You know, "Like if anything happens to me, you just hold on to that band, take care Ella," (inaudible)", you know. I say, "Oh, you'll be all right, don't worry about it." He say, "No, I don't know. You can't never tell, you know, but I'm just telling you." But that is the last time I even had a chance to talk to him. And I was dumbfounded, you know, like when we came back to Baltimore after the Montgomery date was finished down there, we was just walking around Baltimore just like anybody was walking around (inaudible). Ella was following me around, crying and carrying on. I'd walk down the street, she'd be behind me. I was going down Pennsylvania Avenue, bother me I say, "Go on back to the hotel, don't (inaudible)." We stayed in that little hotel and she

We'd walk around the streets. The band was just like -- we just like in a daze like, you know. We were just in a shock.

When we first --

What happened was, when they broke the news to us in Montgomery at that ballroom down there, where we was playing at that big dance, they finally (inaudible) when we got back.

It didn't hit us then, you know. We probably --

When I got back to Baltimore, that's when it really hit. We checked in the hotel and we got there, I think that's when it really took off on all of us, you know.

Because nobody was talking to each other. Nobody. The whole band would -- we just look at each other and just go in and out, you know.

Really, I think that's when the shock really hit the band, when we got back to Baltimore.

Because I remember Ella -- I'd go down
